source_brief: This is a Federal Writers' Project (WPA) life-history interview held by the Library of Congress, catalogued as "Crossing the Plains" (item wpalh001978, also indexed as wpalh2.29091808). It was collected in Oregon, dated April 27, 1939, with Sara B. Wrenn listed as interviewer and Mrs. Jane Lee Smith as the narrator/contributor. The record documents oral memories of an earlier generation's wagon-train migration and pioneer settlement; per its own catalog title, it specifically concerns an encounter with a runaway or aggressive ox among the family's cattle during the crossing. The Library of Congress's public catalog record and search index do not expose the manuscript's full transcribed text, so the precise wording and blow-by-blow details of the ox incident could not be verified from what is accessible; only the framing (a wagon-train migration, an ox/cattle confrontation, told as an oral family memory) is confirmed.
